title: MDA / IMS-MDA / MIDAS
scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic of genomic-DNA multiple displacement amplification and explicitly supported MDA, IMS-MDA and MIDAS contexts. The complete drawn route is Genome → Hybridize primers → two successive illustrations of Phi29 Synthesis, with displacement and secondary priming → S1 nuclease → Amplified DNA. There are no drawn alternative workflow branches; raised DNA branches are molecular intermediates, not separate cell populations. The product shown is amplified genomic DNA, not an adapter-bearing sequencing library. Preserve the diagram’s 3′blocked primer wording as an observation and resolve it from the MDA paper as exonuclease protection with an extendable primer. op_s1 remains a family-level depicted operation with unresolved MDA/IMS-MDA applicability; the supported MIDAS recovery and Polymerase I route is explicitly distinguished as paper-only context. IMS capture and microwell confinement are method distinctions established by primary content, not visual features added to the diagram. The catalogue card contains no method body, so it supplies no additional reaction sequence. No historical development or interchangeability between the named implementations is asserted.

states.label: Extendable, exonuclease-resistant random hexamer primers

states.label: MIDAS unbranched double-stranded DNA for downstream library construction
features: Primary-supported alternative to applying the generic S1 arrow to MIDAS: recovered hyperbranched amplicons are converted using random hexamers and DNA Polymerase I; the methods additionally report nick sealing.
This double-stranded genomic material is the substrate for the paper’s modified Nextera Tn5 library construction. That downstream library operation is outside the drawn amplification schematic.

Downstream library inserts therefore derive from the amplified genome of the recovered cell or nucleus. The paper demonstrates microbial genome assembly and neuronal copy-number measurements; amplification bias still limits interpretation of coverage as original genomic abundance.

method_scopes.rationale: MDA means multiple displacement amplification. The inspected MDA paper supports the random-primer/Phi29 strand-displacement core, including secondary priming on products. The family drawing additionally shows op_s1, but the inspected paper methods and Figure 1 do not establish that arrow as a required step of the scoped MDA implementation. Its applicability is therefore left at family-diagram level rather than added to this method’s operation list. The core architecture is resolved. No sequencing-library preparation is depicted.

method_scopes.rationale: IMS-MDA is a distinct enrichment-plus-amplification implementation, not an alias for plain MDA. In the inspected Chlamydia trachomatis study, antibodies associated with magnetic beads capture intact target bacteria (the reported primary antibody targets LPS); lysis and genomic-DNA denaturation then supply the MDA substrate. Amplification is performed on the retained beads without elution. These upstream context steps distinguish the variant but are not drawn as separate panels. MDA is the shared molecular copying core. Enrichment does not produce a pure target sample, and downstream sequencing can retain contaminant DNA and uneven genome coverage. The protocol PMID 24202554 supplies only abstract-level corroboration of IMS → MDA → sequencing. No supplied primary content establishes the S1 arrow as required for IMS-MDA; its applicability remains unresolved.

method_scopes.rationale: MIDAS means microwell displacement amplification system, a distinct single-cell/nucleus MDA implementation. Limited amplification occurs in individual nanoliter microwells, and selected amplicons are recovered separately; this physical association underlies a cell-specific genomic readout. The shared molecular copying core is shown by the Illumina synthesis panels, but the wells and recovery interface are paper-supported context rather than drawn features. For the sequenced MIDAS products, the paper explicitly reports only one MDA round. The downstream conversion uses random hexamers and DNA Polymerase I to yield unbranched double-stranded DNA before modified Nextera Tn5 library construction; op_s1 is therefore not assigned to this implementation. The two downstream operations in this list are explicitly authored from the primary paper. Sparse loading and amplicon selection support single-cell attribution without making every microwell intrinsically single-cell or every genomic locus equally represented.

corrections.diagram_observation: The primer panel labels the blue short segments with orange terminal marks “3′blocked random hexamer primers”, immediately before Phi29-driven elongation.
corrections.primary_statement: The MDA paper reports thiophosphate-modified random hexamers with 3′-proximal modified linkages and calls the primers exonuclease-resistant; Figure 1 states that these primers initiate DNA synthesis. s_primers is therefore authored as protected, extendable random hexamers. The diagram wording is retained as an observation, interpreted as protection against exonuclease rather than a nonextendable terminal 3′ block.

evidence.rationale: The reported thiophosphate-modified hexamer is used to initiate DNA synthesis in Figure 1. Together with its description as exonuclease-resistant, this supports an extendable primer protected near its 3′ end, rather than a terminal block that prevents polymerase extension. The orange marks alone do not specify a chemical structure.

corrections.diagram_observation: The grouped caption names MIDAS, while the single shared schematic shows S1 nuclease between branched synthesis material and linear amplified-DNA strokes; no variant-specific alternative is drawn.
corrections.primary_statement: The MIDAS full text reports individual-well amplicon recovery, followed by random hexamers and DNA Polymerase I conversion of hyperbranched products into unbranched double-stranded DNA before Tn5 library construction. The MIDAS scope follows that reported route through op_midas_recover and op_midas_convert and excludes op_s1. The S1 operation remains in the family diagram extraction; it is not silently renamed or asserted to be equivalent to Polymerase I conversion.

unknowns.question: Which, if any, specific MDA or IMS-MDA implementation is intended to include the family schematic’s S1 nuclease step? The supplied MDA and IMS-MDA content does not establish this attribution. A method-specific primary statement linking S1 treatment to that implementation would resolve it; MIDAS already has the explicit Polymerase I route. This does not block description of the depicted family-level S1 arrow or the supported copying core.
